boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission activities at the Academy and in Annapolis, with access details from official public sources.

cards.title: Browse the Naval Academy Museum
cards.subtitle: Preble Hall, U.S. Naval Academy
cards.notes: Walk through Preble Hall’s naval-history exhibits together, then leave time to look closely at the ship models and artifacts.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop on the Yard with clearly stated visitor access.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA states that the U.S. Naval Academy Museum is free and ADA accessible.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — U.S. Naval Academy Museum
cards.access_notes: General public pedestrian access is through Gate 1 or Gate 8; visitors 18+ need valid photo ID. Check museum hours and federal-holiday closures before going.

cards.entity_name: U.S. Naval Academy Cemetery and Columbarium
cards.title: Visit the Cemetery and Columbarium
cards.subtitle: Hospital Point, U.S. Naval Academy
cards.notes: Take the mile walk from the Visitor Center to read memorials and use the locator kiosk for a quiet, respectful history stop.
cards.short_summary: A public visitation site on the Academy grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA says the Cemetery and Columbarium are open to public visitation and open for visitation from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Enter through the Visitor Access Center with government-issued Real ID and follow cemetery rules; recreational walking, eating, drinking, biking, and jogging are prohibited there.

cards.title: Attend a public chapel service
cards.subtitle: U.S. Naval Academy Main Chapel
cards.notes: Choose a listed service and attend with friends, allowing extra time for the Gate 1 pedestrian security process and photo-ID check.
cards.short_summary: Public chapel services provide a no-cost, scheduled way to experience the Yard.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA says its Chaplain’s Center holds services open to the public and that public events are free unless otherwise noted.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the service schedule before traveling. Gate access rules apply; visitors 18+ must carry valid photo identification.

cards.title: See Maryland Black-history exhibits
cards.subtitle: 84 Franklin Street, Annapolis
cards.notes: Meet at the museum and move through the exhibits at your own pace, pausing to compare the stories and objects that stand out.
cards.short_summary: Maryland’s official African American heritage museum has free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Annapolis identifies the Banneker-Douglass Museum at 84 Franklin Street and states that admission is free, with donations encouraged.
cards.source_title: A History Lover’s Itinerary — Visit Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The cited visitor information lists Tuesday–Saturday hours; verify current hours with the museum before your visit.

cards.title: Walk the Waterworks Park trails
cards.subtitle: 260 Defense Highway, Annapolis
cards.notes: Bring a friend for the park’s hiking paths, then settle at the picnic area or benches to watch the water and wildlife.
cards.short_summary: A 40-acre city recreation area for a low-key outdoor hang.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Annapolis states Waterworks Park is free of charge, requires no permits, and offers hiking trails, picnic places, and fishing.
cards.access_notes: Use the address provided by the City and follow posted park rules. Any transport or optional equipment is separate from park access.

cards.title: Read the Kunta Kinte-Alex Haley Memorial
cards.subtitle: City Dock, historic Annapolis
cards.notes: Start at the sculpture group, then follow the ten Story Wall markers and finish at the Compass Rose across from Market House.
cards.short_summary: A City Dock memorial with multiple interpretive elements to explore together.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes the memorial’s sculpture group, ten Story Wall markers, and Compass Rose at City Dock.
cards.source_title: About the Memorial — City of Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The memorial is in a City of Annapolis waterfront park; the City’s public-water-access report states all City waterfront parks are free to access.

cards.title: Pause by the waterfront at Susan Campbell Park
cards.subtitle: City Dock, Annapolis
cards.notes: Use the park as a meet-up point for a waterside conversation, then stroll the nearby public dock area without booking an activity.
cards.short_summary: A named City Dock waterfront park for a simple outdoor meet-up.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s City Dock plan identifies Susan Campbell Park as a public recreational space at the waterfront.
cards.source_title: Annapolis City Dock Master Plan — City of Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The City’s public-water-access report states all City of Annapolis waterfront parks are free to access. Parking and boat services may cost extra.

cards.entity_name: Ellen O. Moyer Nature Park at Back Creek
cards.title: Take the Back Creek nature loop
cards.subtitle: Edgewood Road, Annapolis
cards.notes: Walk the park’s trail with a friend, use the benches or pavilion for a break, and keep the visit focused on the natural area.
cards.short_summary: A city nature park with trail and water-access amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s parks listing identifies Ellen O. Moyer Nature Park at Back Creek and lists a bike/hike trail, nature area, pavilion, benches, and water access.
cards.source_title: Amenities at Parks, Trails and Playgrounds — City of Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The City’s public-water-access report states all City waterfront parks are free to access. Use only designated paths and follow posted conditions.

cards.title: Meet up at Carr’s/Elktonia Heritage Park
cards.subtitle: Bembe Beach Road, Annapolis
cards.notes: Plan a daylight waterfront meet-up, then explore the adjacent public park setting and talk through the site’s local cultural history.
cards.short_summary: A named city waterfront park beside the Annapolis Maritime Museum campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Carr’s/Elktonia Heritage Park on Bembe Beach Road as a location for a free, public 2026 Juneteenth celebration.
cards.source_title: Annapolis Juneteenth Celebration Press Release — City of Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The City’s public-water-access report states all City waterfront parks are free to access. Check City notices for any event-related closures or parking limits.

cards.title: Do a State House self-guided visit
cards.subtitle: 100 State Circle, Annapolis
cards.notes: Pick up the self-guided material by the first-floor Archives Room, then compare the building’s historic rooms and civic displays together.
cards.short_summary: A public state building with self-guided visitor information on site.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryland State Archives states that the Maryland State House is open to the public daily and that self-guided tour information is available on the first floor.
cards.source_title: Maryland State House Tours — Maryland State Archives
cards.access_notes: Open 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m. except Christmas and New Year’s Day according to the State Archives; picture ID and metal-detector screening are required.
